result:
My round-3 safety verdict is in `work/board/r0003/safety.json`; it is valid JSON and covers S1–S9. Notes are in `work/agents/safety/r0003_notes.md`. Python could run this round, so every number comes from a script in my folder (`s03`–`s07`, each with its JSON output). All nine constraints should stay.

**Main findings**

1. **Critical: nothing in the bone shape stops the cage sliding toward the spinal cord.** In the model's disc space the gap is narrowest at the front (2.96 mm) and gets taller all the way back (5.30 mm at the back edge of the cage area, 5.48 mm at the disc edge). My round-2 claim that a 0.35 mm "posterior lip" holds the cage was wrong; I took a measurement from a different geometry source. The verdict states the correction.
2. **Critical: the squeeze from the two vertebrae pushes the cage backward on its own.** With even pressure on the real endplate shapes, the cage needs a friction coefficient of 0.08–0.10 just to stay put, before the neck moves at all. That is 41–52 % of the friction available at the low-end value of 0.2. Red-team finding F-0011 gets 0.105 from a simulation, which agrees. I recommend that the friction needed in any backward-pushing load state, including this squeeze-only state, be at most 0.15.
3. **Critical: measuring slip "relative to C3" during load picks up the vertebra's own rotation.** At the 5.78° flexion angle from the solver check, a cage that does not slip at all appears to move 0.62 mm relative to C3. That alone breaks the 0.5 mm backward limit. Net slip should be measured when the load returns to zero after each cycle, and peaks during a cycle against the average position of C3 and C4.
4. **Major: the PI's whole-cage "best-fit" slip measure can hide a hard core moving toward the cord.** In a simple test case, a hard part holding 20 % of the cage's points moved 1.5 mm, but the whole-cage measure read only 0.30 mm. I recommend reporting the larger of the whole-cage value and a hard-core-only value.
5. **Major: `docs/PLAN.md` still has the old insertion rule** ("hard 3 % / soft 40 %"), not the one the PI accepted on 2026-10-27. It also lacks the new slip definition. The constraint-checking code (`constraints.py`) and the `work/requests/` folder for change requests still don't exist; this is the third round I've raised that.

**New items and change requests**
- A new rule S1b: no cage material may end up more than 0.5 mm past the cage area toward the canal or the sides under load.
- A checklist for designs that expand or latch after insertion. The key point is that if the mechanism fails to open, the cage must still not slide toward the cord.
- A check on why two geometry sources disagree on the back disc height (4.1 mm vs 5.48 mm). This decides whether any shape stop toward the cord is possible at all.
- A check of facet-joint load at the 2 mm insertion distraction.
- The items the PI deferred on 2026-10-27 are recorded in the verdict, not re-argued.

**Friction:** I still found no measured value for PLCL or PLA on vertebral bone. The only direct polymer-on-bone study is Zhang et al. 2023 (PEEK on cortical bone), and its abstract gives no number. Published cage simulations assume values of 0.2–0.4. I kept the PI's 0.3 main value (0.2 / 0.45 for comparison), with the backward direction judged at 0.2. The Europe PMC literature database was down for part of the session, so that search is incomplete.

The squeeze figure (finding 2) assumes even pressure across the cage faces. It should be replaced by the friction-limit calculation (`e02`) once that handles curved faces and is run on real simulation results.

Sources:
- [Damm et al. 2015, J Biomech](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jbiomech.2015.07.012)
- [Zhang et al. 2023, Macromol Biosci](https://doi.org/10.1002/mabi.202200548)
- [BMC Musculoskelet Disord 2020, cage simulation study (friction 0.2 assumed)](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12891-020-03411-1)
- [Hsueh et al. 2023, Sci Rep](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-023-44998-4)
